issues.legal_issue: Immediate delivery of possession should not be ordered while a related declaratory suit concerning the occupant’s claimed rights remains pending.
material_facts: An eviction decree had been granted and affirmed, including on the ground of unlawful subletting, but it had not been executed.
The occupant obstructed delivery of possession and claimed rights as a tenant through a party to the eviction proceedings.
The occupant had filed a declaratory suit concerning those claimed rights, and that suit remained pending.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to direct immediate delivery of possession while the declaratory suit remained pending and did not express an opinion on the merits of the parties’ contentions in that suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered it inappropriate to order possession at that stage while the occupant’s declaratory suit was pending. The judgment cites no earlier cases or specific statutory provision as the basis for that decision; it recounts that an execution application had been made under Order XXI Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

predicates.eviction_decree_unexecuted: A party obtained an eviction decree, but delivery of possession under it has not occurred.
predicates.occupant_claims_rights: The person in possession obstructed enforcement and asserted a right to remain in the property.
predicates.related_declaratory_suit_pending: The person in possession filed a suit seeking a declaration of the asserted rights, and that suit remains pending.

issues.definition: When an eviction decree remains unexecuted, the occupant asserts rights to remain, and a related declaratory suit is pending, immediate possession is not ordered.

issues.legal_issue: A person remaining in possession during delayed enforcement of an eviction decree may be directed to pay interim compensation to protect the decree-holder from continuing injury.
material_facts: The eviction decree had remained unexecuted for a lengthy period.
The occupant continued to hold the property and claimed to have obtained possession through a party against whom the eviction decree had been made.
The occupant’s declaratory suit remained pending, so the Court did not resolve the merits of the claimed tenancy rights.
The decree-holder sought possession and payment for the period during which the property was held.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the occupants to pay mesne profits or compensation at the rates it specified, with prior payments adjusted and arrears paid in instalments.
issues.legal_principle: To protect a judgment creditor from continuing injury when enforcement of a decree for possession is delayed, a court may order reasonable mesne profits or compensation, which may be equivalent to market rent. In an appropriate case, it may appoint a receiver and require the person holding the property to act as the receiver’s agent and deposit a fixed royalty, or make another suitable order. No earlier cases or specific statutory provision are cited as the basis for these principles.

rule.if: decree_execution_proceeding and eviction_decree_unexecuted and person_holds_property and enforcement_delay_continues

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a decree for possession of property.
predicates.eviction_decree_unexecuted: A party obtained an eviction decree, but delivery of possession under it has not occurred.
predicates.person_holds_property: A person other than the decree-holder continues to possess the property.
predicates.enforcement_delay_continues: Enforcement of the decree has been delayed while the person continues to hold the property.

issues.definition: In a possession-decree enforcement proceeding, if the decree remains unexecuted, another person holds the property, and enforcement is delayed, interim occupation compensation is ordered.

issues.legal_issue: A related pending declaratory suit should be disposed of expeditiously when its pendency delays resolution of a property-possession dispute arising from an unexecuted eviction decree.
material_facts: An eviction decree had not been executed, and the occupant’s claim to rights in the property was being pursued in a declaratory suit.
The declaratory suit remained pending while the parties disputed possession and compensation.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed that the declaratory suit be disposed of as expeditiously as possible, preferably within one year.
issues.legal_principle: The Court issued a case-management direction for expeditious disposal in view of the prolonged proceedings and the pending suit concerning the occupant’s asserted rights. It cited no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this direction.

predicates.eviction_decree_unexecuted: A party obtained an eviction decree, but delivery of possession under it has not occurred.
predicates.related_declaratory_suit_pending: The person in possession filed a suit seeking a declaration of the asserted rights, and that suit remains pending.
predicates.possession_dispute_continues: The decree-holder and the person in possession continue to dispute who is entitled to possession of the property.

issues.definition: When an eviction decree remains unexecuted, a related declaratory suit is pending, and the possession dispute continues, the related suit is directed for expeditious disposal.
